title: Is South Africa v New Zealand on TV? Channel, kick-off time and how to watch second Test
description: Everything you need to know as the Springboks and All Blacks clash in Cape Town
fullText:
South Africa will look to hit back in the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry series after New Zealand went 1-0 up with victory at Ellis Park.

A tremendous performance from the All Blacks saw them turn over their hosts 33-16 in the first Test, and another win here would ensure that Dave Rennie's side cannot be beaten in this four-match series.

The Springboks have recalled some of their most experienced figures, though. as Rassie Erasmus seeks a reaction from his squad as the tour relocates to Cape Town.

Another captivating contest could well be in store as this landmark series continues.

Here's everything you need to know.

The second Test is due to kick off at 4.10pm BST on Saturday 29 August at Cape Town Stadium.

Viewers in the United Kingdom can watch every game from the Rugby's Greatest Rivalry tour live on Sky Sports, while South African viewers can tune in via SuperSport.

Siya Kolisi returns to captain the Springboks having been left out of the first Test squad, while Handre Pollard had originally been named at fly half before suffering a niggle in training. Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu therefore retains the No 10 shirt, with Cheslin Kolbe also brought in to the starting side on Friday at Kurt-Lee Arendse's expense.

The 39-year-old Deon Fourie is primed for his first international appearance since the 2023 World Cup final after being named as hooking cover for Malcolm Marx.

South Africa XV: 1 Ox Nche, 2 Malcolm Marx, 3 Wilco Louw; 4 Eben Etzebeth, 5 Ruan Nortje; 6 Siya Kolisi (capt.), 7 Pieter-Steph du Toit, 8 Jasper Wiese; 9 Cobus Reinach, 10 Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu; 11 Ethan Hooker, 12 Damian de Allende, 13 Jesse Kriel, 14 Cheslin Kolbe; 15 Damian Willemse.

Replacements: 16 Deon Fourie, 17 Gerhard Steenekamp, 18 Thomas du Toit, 19 Lood de Jager, 20 Andre Esterhuizen, 21 Cameron Hanekom; 22 Morne van den Berg, 23 Manie Libbok.

New Zealand are forced into two tight five changes after Ethan de Groot and Josh Lord suffered head injuries in the first Test. George Bower steps in for the former having impressed at loosehead off the bench, while Tupou Vaa'i slides a row forward from blindside to lock as Fabian Holland's partner.

Simon Parker is therefore brought in on the flank, while Leroy Carter is preferred to Josh Moorby on the left wing.

title: ‘I’m Not Drinking The Kool-Aid Anymore’ — 2-Time Super Bowl Champion WR Completely Turns on Colorado HC Deion Sanders in Fiery Rant
description: Deion Sanders is healthy and focused on helping Colorado rebound from its three-win campaign in 2025. Coach Prime made several roster changes during the offseason in an effort to turn things around, but two-time Super Bowl champion Brandon Stokley remains skeptical about the Buffaloes’ potential.
fullText:
Deion Sanders is healthy and focused on helping Colorado rebound from its three-win campaign in 2025.

Coach Prime made several roster changes during the offseason in an effort to turn things around, but two-time Super Bowl champion Brandon Stokley remains skeptical about the Buffaloes' potential.

Sanders inherited a Colorado program that had gone 1-11 in 2022 and immediately sparked plenty of excitement in his first season. The Buffaloes opened 2023 with a 3-0 record but ultimately finished 4-8, losing eight of their final nine games.

The Buffaloes bounced back in 2024, posting a 9-4 record and becoming one of the most-watched teams in college football. More than 54 million viewers watched Colorado games throughout the 2024 season.

However, Colorado took a major step back in 2025, finishing 3-9 after losing Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter to the NFL.

While quarterback Julian Lewis seems to be showing promise heading into the 2026 season, and footage from the Colorado locker room has fueled optimism about the team's potential, Stokley remains skeptical.

"I'm not drinking the Kool-Aid anymore," Stokley said. "I'm not. Sorry, I was hook, line, and sinker. I loved it when Deion was here when they hired him… That was awesome. The energy, the buzz, the excitement-that was fun… You know what wasn't fun? Last year.

"And then you look at, oh, you're paying him $10 million, but then you look at it's just nonstop chatter, nonstop talk. I'm tired of it. You haven't backed up anything. What have you backed up? And it's just all spin. It's like he just throws stuff out there."

There's been noise around the Sanders family for varying reasons this year.

Coach Prime found himself involved in a legal matter surrounding his son, Shilo Sanders. A federal bankruptcy judge ruled on Aug. 27 that the Colorado head coach must be available to testify remotely in Shilo's upcoming bankruptcy trial at 1:30 p.m. MT on Sept. 4, one day after Colorado begins its season against Georgia Tech.

The judge clarified that Sanders would only need to appear if rebuttal testimony becomes necessary. However, Stokley also questioned the way the situation has been portrayed publicly.

DON'T MISS:'Get Good Or Get Gone': Broncos Legend Serves Colorado HC Deion Sanders a Cold, Hard Reality Check

"All of a sudden, you know, Shilo's situation," Stokley added. "He's trying to say Shilo won. Shilo didn't win. Shilo owes $12 million. That's not a win. So you're spending things to make us think that we're not very bright. And I'm just over that whole situation."

Shilo filed for bankruptcy in October 2023 in an effort to discharge more than $11 million in debt. Almost all of that amount is owed to John Darjean, a former security guard at his school in Dallas, who is the plaintiff in the bankruptcy case.

title: Jürgen Klopp says he didn’t talk to Bayern Munich star Jamal Musiala, he sent him a voice memo
description: The Germany boss wants FC Bayern’s Jamal Musiala to get healthy.
fullText:
Jürgen Klopp has offered Jamal Musiala a strong message of support as the Bayern Munich star continues to deal with his latest setback, making it clear that his place in the Germany national team will not be affected by his rehabilitation.

Speaking about his communication with Musiala, Klopp explained that he did not actually call the 23-year-old directly, instead choosing to send him a voice message.

"We didn't speak on the phone. I sent him a voice message. He doesn't know me at all and doesn't have my number. I think if I had called him, he wouldn't have answered for three days because he wouldn't have recognized my number. He responded to the message. He's in a situation that you wouldn't wish on anyone, especially not a young guy like him. But everything should turn out fine, everyone agrees on that. I reassured him that this wouldn't have any impact on the national team," Klopp told Sky Germany (as captured by @iMiaSanMia)."That's all I can do for him. Vincent Kompany confirmed to me that he was in incredible shape. After the metal plate and screws were removed, he was back to his old self, or even better. Now this has happened for the reasons we know.

"What's important now is that he is given the necessary time, and that he gives himself that time as well. Young players normally don't have any problems, apart from becoming impatient, and of course you can't afford to be impatient during a phase like this. He's at the perfect club, in the perfect environment for that, and we also want to do our part. And we're telling him: 'Son, first get healthy, and then the door is open for you.'"

For Bayern Munich, Klopp's comments should provide plenty of encouragement. Musiala's priority remains getting healthy and allowing himself the necessary time to recover rather than rushing his return.

The fact that Klopp has already reassured him that Germany's door remains open is another important message for the Bayern Munich star.

Musiala has already established himself as one of Germany's most important players, and Klopp clearly intends to make him a central part of his plans once he is ready to return.

For now, however, the message from Klopp is exactly what Musiala needs to hear — get healthy first, and everything else can wait.

title: Former Braves Pitcher Punches, Pins Knife-Wielding Man To Protect Players, Per Report
description: “I don’t think I’m a hero,” the former Atlanta Braves right-hander said, shortly after subduing an intoxicated man in a hotel, according to police.
fullText:
The Atlanta Braves have employed countless players throughout their long history, from Hall of Fame stars to short-term contributors whose careers in Atlanta were measured in only a handful of appearances.

Kevin Lomon belongs in the latter category, pitching briefly for the Braves in 1996 during a major league career that ultimately lasted just 12 games. Lomon made six relief appearances for Atlanta that season, working seven-and-one-third innings with a 4.91 ERA. He allowed seven hits and three walks while striking out one batter, with his final major league appearance coming on Sept. 28, 1996.

Overall, Lomon pitched 16 2/3 innings, surrendering 24 hits and eight walks while recording seven strikeouts in his career. But nearly three decades later, he has made headlines for a heroic reaction to a violent threat.

Cubs' 2-Year Veteran, Former ROTY And All-Star, Cuts Ties With New Team After Just 3 Games

Lomon is now the head baseball coach at Cameron High School in southeastern Oklahoma. Earlier this month, he was traveling with 13 players for a baseball game in Shawnee when an alarming situation unfolded at the team's hotel.

"An Oklahoma high school baseball coach says he didn't have much time to think when one of his players called from a hotel room saying a man had pulled a knife," Taylor Howard reported for 5 CBS News.

Lomon said that one of his players called him around 9 p.m. after encountering a man in the hotel hallway. The player reported that the man had opened a knife and moved toward him before retreating into his room.

Lomon instructed his players to get inside their rooms and called 911. He then went into the hallway himself.

The police report indicated that Lomon encountered the man near the elevators with an open knife. The man allegedly moved toward Lomon, who punched him several times before holding him on the ground until police arrived.

Yankees' Survivor 51 Contestant Sends Brian Cashman Message In Debut Video

The confrontation ended without physical injuries being reported among Lomon or his players. Police reportedly recovered two knives, while Stevens was arrested on complaints of assault with a deadly weapon and public intoxication, according to Howard.

For Lomon, the decision was less about bravery than responsibility.

"I don't think I'm a hero," Lomon said, per Howard. "I just think I would do it again."

That mindset reflects the role he has embraced long after his brief MLB career ended. As a coach responsible for 13 young players on the road, Lomon viewed protecting them as part of his job.

His former life as a Braves pitcher may have lasted only part of one season, but nearly 30 years later, Lomon found himself facing another high-pressure situation — this time with his young team depending on him to keep them safe.

title: Chiefs Finish Winless Preseason With 9-9 Tie vs. Seahawks
description: The Kansas City Chiefs once again featured field goals in their final preseason game against Seattle.
fullText:
The Kansas City Chiefs finished their uninspiring preseason with a 9-9 tie against the Seattle Seahawks, as Seattle kicker Jason Myers missed a 52-yard field goal that would have won the game as time expired.

The tie meant the Chiefs went winless during the preseason with an 0-2-1, which wasn't surprsing given that they scored just a single touchdown in three games.

Both teams sat their starting quarterbacks, as per usual in the third preseason game, with Seattle keeping Sam Darnold on the sidelines and the Chiefs playing without Patrick Mahomes as he continues to shoot for Week 1 while rehabiliting his knee after offseason surgery.

Just two quarterbacks played in this one, with Garrett Nussmeier going 22-for-34 for 198 yards for Kansas City and Jalen Milroe going 16-for-26 for Seattle.

The first half was a battle of field goals with the Chiefs getting a pair of Harrison Butker chip shots from less than 30 yards, while Myers had one from 46 yards out to make it 6-3 at halftime.

Seattle scored the lone touchdown of the game in the third quarter on a four-yard pass from Milroe to Nick Vanett, but Myers missed the extra point to make it 9-6. Kansas City then tied the game at 9-9 on another short field goal from Butker to make it 9-9, and Seattle's final drive stalled to force the missed field goal that left it a tie.

Chiefs linebacker R Mason Thomas had a strip sack and a fumble recover, and he probably expressed the thoughts about the possibility of bonus preseason football.

"I thought we were going to overtime," he said in an ESPN/AP report, "but it was nice to get a tie."

Thomas was more excited about the Chiefs opener against the Denver Broncos at Arrowhead on Sept. 14, as it will be the first game of the season featured on Monday Night Football.

"It's going to be packed out, at night in the loudest stadium in the in the whole NFL," Thomas added. "I'm excited."

The Chiefs did get several noteworthy performance despite their overall sluggish offense. Andrew Armstrong caught five passes for 52 yards in his bid to make roster, and rookie running back had a nice game with 39 yards on seven carries for a 5.6 yards per carry average.

Brashard Smith had 72 yards on 16 carries as running back Kenneth Walker III sat out this one after sustaining a foot injury in practice during the week.

title: Scottie Scheffler comments on what Ludvig Aberg is really like as a playing partner
description: Scottie Scheffler played alongside Ludvig Aberg during the second round of the Tour Championship on Friday. Scheffler posted a solid second-round 67, while Aberg carded a 68 at East Lake.
fullText:
Scottie Scheffler played alongside Ludvig Aberg during the second round of the Tour Championship on Friday.

Scheffler posted a solid second-round 67, while Aberg carded a 68 at East Lake.

The 30-year-old world number one is just two strokes adrift of the lead heading into the weekend, with the Swede a further shot back.

While Scottie Scheffler and Ludvig Aberg would both prefer to be leading, they will be happy with their positions after two rounds of the Tour Championship.

Aberg enjoyed playing with Scheffler on day two at the Tour Championship, with both players moving at a good pace around East Lake.

Now Scheffler has opened up on what Aberg is like to play alongside.

Scheffler spoke to the media at East Lake late on Friday night after a practice session alongside his coach Randy Smith.

The world number one was asked what Ludvig Aberg was like to play with on day two of the Tour Championship.

"He's an easy guy to get paired with," Scheffler replied.

"He's a really nice guy. He's a great competitor, good player as well. He's always very easy to be on the golf course with.

"It's pretty simple to be paired with him."

Scheffler is paired with Cam Young for the third round of the Tour Championship, while Aberg will play alongside Adam Scott.

Scheffler has missed both tee shots out to the right on the opening hole this week, and has been forced to lay up both times on the long par-four.

During the final round of the Tour Championship in 2025, Scheffler actually hit his opening drive out of bounds to the left.

And he was asked after his second round yesterday if the right miss is now in his head.

"I mean, there's an out-of-bounds fence on the left," he said.

"Didn't really hit too bad of a shot there. Then you get a lie there that you can't advance more than 80 yards.

"No, I wouldn't say anything is in my head out there. Thank you, though."

title: Jose Mourinho sees only one position for Real Madrid captain
description: As Real Madrid’s captain, Federico Valverde has been one of the first names on the team sheet for several years now. Yet, he has barely ever stayed fixated on a single position.Despite being one of ...
fullText:
As Real Madrid's captain, Federico Valverde has been one of the first names on the team sheet for several years now. Yet, he has barely ever stayed fixated on a single position.

Despite being one of the team's most important players over the years, the Uruguayan star has been used as a Swiss-knife by manager after manager who have all praised him for his versatility.

As a result, he has played as a full-back, a defensive midfielder, an attacking midfielder and even a winger based on the requirement of the team.

As reported by MARCA, the new Real Madrid manager Jose Mourinho is not a fan of Valverde being used all over the field. He sees the player as a midfielder and a midfielder only, specifically a deep-lying midfielder at that.

Valverde has started the season well. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images)

The player, after all, has started off the team's games so far this season and has played as part of the double pivot on both nights alongside Bernardo Silva. He has enjoyed a strong start to the season, and his numbers speak volumes.

Against Real Sociedad, the player made three defensive actions, two recoveries and one interception.

He was not dribbled past in the entire game, won two duels and completed 93% of his passes. Beyond his defensive numbers, he assisted Kylian Mbappe and had two shots on goal.

It is clear at this point that Mourinho sees Valverde only as a midfielder, especially since he now has convincing options at full-back and on the right wing.

How will Mourinho incorporate Tchouameni? (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images)

The central midfield is where the manager sees the player's output to be the highest.

Part of the reason why Valverde has had a non-turbulent start to the season, however, is the injury Aurelien Tchouameni is suffering from.

The Frenchman has been the club's de facto pivot player for a long time now and was expected to be the manager's preferred option to partner Silva in the double pivot.

His absence helped the Uruguayan earn Mourinho's favour and move up the pecking order. Tchouameni's return, however, is not far off and it remains to be seen how the selection changes after he is back in action.

title: Updated De’Zhaun Stribling Fantasy Outlook 2026: Is the 49ers Rookie a Diamond in the Rough?
description: De’Zhaun Stribling enters the 2026 season with a clear path to targets following extensive roster turnover and injuries in the 49ers’ offense. While he is not a plug-and-play fantasy starter for Week 1, his impressive preseason performance makes him a high-upside depth piece with midseason breakout potential as a rookie.
fullText:
De'Zhaun Stribling enters the 2026 season with a clear path to targets following extensive roster turnover and injuries in the 49ers' offense. While he is not a plug-and-play fantasy starter for Week 1, his impressive preseason performance makes him a high-upside depth piece with midseason breakout potential as a rookie.

Stribling turned heads during the summer, catching 11 of his 13 targets for 109 yards through the first two weeks of the preseason after generating plenty of buzz at camp. That strong summer performance has been a sight for sore eyes in San Francisco, a team battling the injury bug before a single live bullet is fired.

Ricky Pearsall (PCL) is out for the season, creating a vacancy in the receiving rotation from the jump. Meanwhile, veteran Mike Evans has his best football behind him, and Deebo Samuel enters the year after the NFL essentially told us that his time as a viable asset is nearly over after no team showed interest until August.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

Christian Kirk is coming off an inefficient season and has struggled to remain on the field, though I'm not sold he was destined to be a real piece of this offense anyway. While George Kittle continues to make great strides, his playing style and age is a tough combination to feel great about over the four-plus month grid that is the NFL regular season.

This leaves the offense in a last-man-standing situation. Christian McCaffrey and Kittle will certainly absorb a significant share of the targets, but they can't carry the entire passing attack on their own. When the front office drafted Stribling, the move was widely viewed by most as a reach. That selection proved the organization was significantly higher on his prospect profile than the general scouting public, and his summer has only reinforced those internal beliefs.

Playing in a Kyle Shanahan system led by Brock Purdy provides Stribling with upside in the efficiency department, as that tandem ranks among the most consistent in football.

For me, he represents a smart process buy in drafts. You should not rely on him as a weekly fantasy starter right away, but once your starting lineup is filled, he serves as a viable depth target who could realistically transition into a weekly lineup staple by the middle of the season.

The price is on the rise, so be careful, but there seems to be some fire at the bottom of this preseason smoke.

title: Broncos kicker Wil Lutz close to hitting impressive PAT streak
description: Denver Broncos kicker Wil Lutz is one extra point away from 100 consecutive converted PATs.
fullText:
There isn't anything flashy about Denver Broncos placekicker Wil Lutz. He doesn't have the strongest leg in the NFL and his name won't come up when fantasy football players want the league's top kicker. But one thing he has proven to be is consistent.

Consistency is exactly what coach Sean Payton was looking for when he traded for Lutz, his former kicker in New Orleans. That consistency also helped Lutz get a three-year contract extension from the team last year.

Lutz has currently made 99 consecutive PATs for the team, something that is no longer a given in today's game. Several teams have cycled through multiple kickers over the last several years, while the Broncos have had just one guy, whose job security is not threatened.

"[I have] a lot of pride, and I don't mind talking about it," Lutz said of his streak. "I think it's a cool feature. This game is decided by, if you look at the stats, it's like something like 75 percent of games are decided by three points. So I take just as much pride in the extra point as I do a 55-yarder in the third quarter. It's important.

"I think you saw in the Giants game, one point changes the entire approach of the game. So that comes from preparation and not having a lazy swing in those moments. It's the kick you're going to hit the most in the season. So it's making sure you're locked in for all 70, 60 extra points you're going to have. Hopefully we can keep that going."

Lutz referenced the wild comeback the Broncos had against the New York Giants last season, in which Giants kicker Jude McAtamney missed two extra-point kicks in that game, which the Broncos won 33-32.

Lutz's streak of 99 straight makes is the top active streak in the league. Tyler Bass of the Buffalo Bills made 104 straight from 2020 to 2022. Justin Tucker made 112 straight for the Baltimore Ravens from 2015 to 2018.

The all-time NFL record, which will likely never be touched, is 523 in a row, held by Stephen Gostkowski of the New England Patriots between 2006 and 2016. However, most of those kicks were made from the old 20-yard range, where you rarely ever saw a miss. The league changed it to a 33-yard kick in 2015, which changed the success rate quite a bit.

If he makes his first PAT attempt this season, Lutz will hit 100 makes in a row, which is certainly an impressive achievement.

title: You’re going to see some absurdly long field goals in the NFL this season. Here’s why
description: Last season, Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little drilled a 68-yard field goal that became the longest field goal ever made in an NFL game. That kick was actually shorter than the 70-yarder he hit during the preseason. Then, just last week, Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker hit a 69-yarder of his own. Absurdly long…
fullText:
Last season, Jacksonville Jaguars kicker Cam Little drilled a 68-yard field goal that became the longest field goal ever made in an NFL game. That kick was actually shorter than the 70-yarder he hit during the preseason. Then, just last week, Kansas City Chiefs kicker Harrison Butker hit a 69-yarder of his own.

Absurdly long field goals are becoming a pattern in the NFL, and it's almost surely going to continue this year.

Over the past few seasons, the NFL has quietly made some changes to its kicking balls that seem to have made things noticeably easier on kickers. That, coupled with the recent kickoff changes that have made a drastic impact on starting field position, has led to an increase in incredibly long field goals.

Ahead of the 2025 season, the NFL quietly passed a resolution that allowed teams to prepare their kicking balls – known in the league as "K-balls" – before game day, rather than during game day. The change got very little publicity, likely because nobody really expected the change to make a drastic difference. But it seems to have, and Philadelphia Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio took notice.

Following a game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in which kicker Chase McLaughlin hit a 65-yard field goal and a 58-yard field goal, Fangio brought up the quiet rule change, saying that it made a "drastic" impact on the kicking game. Fangio said the impact has been so drastic that he compared it to the steroid era of Major League Baseball.

"You know what you guys have missed? Not just you but everybody is, we gave up a 65-yard field goal and a 58-yard field goal," he told reporters via ESPN. "These kicking balls that changed this year, have drastically changed the kicking game, field goals in particular. It's almost like they need an asterisk era, like it was the live ball era, or the asterisk for those home runs that [Barry] Bonds or [Sammy] Sosa or [Mark] McGwire were hitting. The way they have changed the ball, the NFL has drastically changed the field goals."

The new rules allow teams to break in the balls throughout the week rather than just in the minutes leading up to the game, which allows for the ball to fly a bit further, anonymous special teams coordinators told ESPN.

"The ball is flying 5 yards further because the balls are broken in well," an anonymous special teams coordinator told ESPN in a text message.

The data doesn't lie, either. In 2024, kickers made just four of 14 attempts beyond 60 yards – just 29%. In 2025, that number jumped to 12 of 22 – 55%. And it sounds like the league is happy with those results, especially when it leads to exciting, game-ending long field goals.

"After four weeks, I've walked out of here at the Art McNally Gameday Central, like, damn, we had three walk-off field goals today!" NFL executive vice president of football operations Troy Vincent said. "And it's not just walk-off. They're not like they are 30 yards, they are kicking that thing from 50-plus, and they're walking off."

While the new rules for the kicking balls have seemingly made it easier for kickers to connect from long distances, the new kickoff rules will likely give them more opportunities.

Beginning in 2024, the NFL moved to its new dynamic kickoff format. While the league said that the new kickoff format was designed to increase the number of kickoff returns while minimizing the number of high-speed collisions, the change has also had another consequence: a drastic improvement in starting field position.

Under the new format, a touchback results in the offense taking possession at the 35-yard line, up 10 yards from the 25-yard line. Additionally, the new kickoff format has produced some longer returns on average. As a result, the average starting field position is up dramatically, from the 25.6-yard line to the 30.6-yard line.

That's obviously had an impact on scoring, as better starting field position leads to more scoring opportunities. It also has the potential to increase long field goals.

The NFL has no shortage of kickers who can reliably connect from long range – guys like Little, Butker, McLaughlin, Evan McPherson, Brandon Aubrey, just to name a few. If the range for those players is now on their own side of the field thanks to the new kicking balls, offenses are now just a play or two away from field goal range before they even step onto the field, thanks to the new kickoff format.

As teams and kickers gradually realize that field goal range is longer than it's ever been and they have more chances at these long kicks than ever before, expect to see a drastic increase in absurdly long field goal attempts this season and beyond.

title: Sunderland Plot Hijack Move For Lyon Winger Malick Fofana Amid Igor Paixão Saga
description: Sunderland have been credited with interest in Lyon winger Malick Fofana, who has been linked with Hull City and Roma, amid their ongoing pursuit of Marseille winger Igor Paixão.
fullText:
Sunderland have been linked with transfer interest in Lyon winger Malick Fofana within the summer transfer window amid the Black Cats' ongoing pursuit of Marseille star Igor Paixão.

Ahead of Sunderland's home clash versus Fulham, reports emerged from Foot Mercato journalist Santi Aouna on X that Sunderland are weighing up a move for 21-year-old talent Fofana.

Sunderland are said to be exploring the potential move for Belgium international Fofana while discussions with Marseille for Paixão hit stumbling blocks over the financial aspects of the transfer, despite reports from Fabrizio Romano suggesting that the Brazilian has agreed personal terms with the Stadium of Light outfit.

In regard to Fofana, the report outlines that Premier League new boys Hull City have verbally offered £30m for the youngster, with Serie A giants Roma also said to have a contractual agreement in place with the Lyon starlet.

Lyon signed Fofana from Belgian giants KAA Gent for a near £17m fee back in the summer of 2023, and the left-winger has gone on to score 19 goals and notch six assists in 83 outings for the Ligue 1 outfit.

Fofana's return is impressive considering that he is still in the developmental stages of his career, with his technical ceiling and potential seeing the likes of Premier League powerhouses Liverpool, Chelsea and Arsenal credited with interest in the promising young winger last summer.

Already this season, Fofana has netted twice in five outings for Lyon, with a goal in their 2-0 win over Toulouse in their Ligue 1 opener, and in his side's recent 2-1 Champions League qualification defeat to Turkish outfit Fenerbahçe.

From a red-and-white perspective, it is clear to see why Sunderland are interested in the Lyon starlet, given how much potential and prowess the pacey winger possesses.

However, the interest in Fofana could potentially be a smokescreen to ramp up the pressure on Marseille to push forward the timeline of the prospective Paixão transfer, given the current wingers that Le Bris' Sunderland squad has to offer.

Sunderland wingers Nilson Angulo and Chemsdine Talbi are of similar profiles to Fofana in terms of being promising young talents, but 26-year-old Paixão would theoretically be a more experienced talent ready to make an immediate impact on the Black Cats' attacking output in wide areas.

Paixão, who netted 12 goals and notched six assists in 42 outings for Marseille last season in his debut campaign for the financially struggling Ligue 1 side, would seemingly be Sunderland's current priority target over Fofana for a recruit out wide.

Now, it remains to be seen whether Sunderland's move for Paixão will materialise, or they will pursue with the reported interest in £30m Fofana and deal an unforseen transfer blow on Hull and Roma.

title: Red Wings move into first-place tie behind fourth-inning rally
description: Liover Peguero drove in three runs as the Red Wings climbed into a first-place tie.
fullText:
The Rochester Red Wings continued their postseason push Friday night, rallying from an early two-run deficit to beat the Buffalo Bisons 5-3 at ESL Ballpark and move into a tie for first place in the International League's second-half standings.

Rochester improved to 79-49 and pulled even with Indianapolis atop the International League's second-half race thanks to a four-run fourth inning fueled by doubles from Cayden Wallace and Liover Peguero. Chandler Champlain earned the win with 4.1 innings of relief before Yovanny Cruz recorded his fifth save.

The Bisons broke through in the top of the fourth inning after Yohendrick Piñango singled and scored on Jay Harry's RBI double. Harry later came home on Lenyn Sosa's RBI single, giving Buffalo a 2-0 lead.

Starter Isaac Lyon was charged with both runs, with Champlain entering in relief to record the final out of the inning.

The Red Wings responded immediately in the bottom half.

Phillip Glasser worked a leadoff walk and Yohandy Morales followed with a single. After a flyout, Wallace lined an RBI double to center field to cut the deficit to one run. Following a walk to Leandro Pineda and a pitching change, Peguero delivered the biggest hit of the night, a three-run double that scored Morales, Wallace and Pineda to put Rochester ahead 4-2.

Buffalo trimmed the lead to 4-3 in the fifth when Sean Keys tripled home Josh Smith.

The Red Wings got that run back in the bottom of the inning. Glasser singled, Morales followed with another hit, and after Morales stole second base, Wallace grounded out to bring Glasser home and extend the lead to 5-3.

That proved to be the final run of the game.

Champlain settled things after Buffalo's fourth-inning rally, allowing just one run on two hits while striking out six across 4.1 innings to earn his eighth win.

Cruz worked a scoreless ninth inning, striking out two while stranding a leadoff double by Harry to secure the save.

Peguero: 2-for-3, double, three RBIs, walk, stolen base.

Wallace: 1-for-4, double, two RBIs.

Morales: 2-for-4, one runs scored, stolen base.

Glasser: 1-for-3, two runs scored, walk.

Champlain (W, 8-5): 4.1 IP, 2 H, 1 ER, 3 BB, 6 K.

The Red Wings continue their series against Buffalo with games scheduled for Saturday and Sunday.

title: Red Sox Face Daunting Doubleheader Challenge Against Yankees Aces
description: After being shut out in consecutive games, the Red Sox must find an offensive answer against Carlos Rodón and returning Yankees ace Max Fried.
fullText:
Red Sox Face Daunting Doubleheader Challenge Against Yankees Aces originally appeared on NESN. 

The Boston Red Sox could not solve Cam Schlittler on Friday night. Their reward is a Saturday date with two of the New New York Yankees' top pitchers.

New York will activate Max Fried from the injured list to start the second game of Saturday's doubleheader at Yankee Stadium. Carlos Rodón will start the opener against Red Sox left-hander Connelly Early.

Fried's return comes exactly 15 days after the Yankees placed him on the injured list, allowing him to return following a minimum-length absence. The timing presents another difficult test for Boston's struggling lineup.

The Red Sox entered Saturday after being shut out in consecutive games. They dropped Friday's series opener 1-0 despite recording five hits and drawing six walks against New York's pitching staff. Boston went 0-for-9 with runners in scoring position and stranded 10 runners. The loss extended its scoreless streak to 18 innings.

Rodón and Fried give the Yankees a pair of accomplished left-handed starters for a doubleheader with significant American League playoff implications.

Fried will return to the rotation for the nightcap after initially expressing hope that his injured-list stay would be brief. The Yankees confirmed his scheduled start following Friday's victory, according to Pinstripe Alley.

The Red Sox first must deal with Rodón.

Boston will send Early to the mound in the opener and likely will need another strong pitching performance after wasting Patrick Sandoval's excellent start Friday. Sandoval allowed only one run on three hits over 5 1/3 innings, but Paul Goldschmidt's solo home run was enough to decide the game.

MORE: How to Watch Red Sox vs. Yankees Doubleheader: Channels, Live Streams & Start Times for Saturday MLB Games

Boston's offense has created opportunities during its current drought. Finishing them has been the problem. Ceddanne Rafaela and Wilyer Abreu combined for four of the Red Sox's five hits Friday. The rest of the lineup went 1-for-24, including hitless nights from Willson Contreras, Adley Rutschman, Jarren Duran and Nick Sogard.

Reinforcements could be approaching. Roman Anthony and Trevor Story reportedly completed their rehab assignments with Triple-A Worcester and are expected to join the team in New York. Both could be activated Saturday or Sunday, according to MLB reporter Francys Romero.

Whether either player returns in time for the doubleheader remains unclear.

What is clear is that Boston's margin for error continues to shrink. The Red Sox fell three games behind the Yankees with Friday's loss and now must rediscover their offense against Rodón and a returning Fried.

title: Updated Romeo Doubs Fantasy Outlook 2026: Patriots WR Worth Targeting After Fresh Start?
description: Romeo Doubs has produced almost the exact same fantasy season three years running without ever generating any excitement. A move to New England finally gets him out of the receiver rotation that defined his career in Green Bay.
fullText:
Romeo Doubs has produced almost the exact same fantasy season three years running without ever generating any excitement. A move to New England finally gets him out of the receiver rotation that defined his career in Green Bay. He now steps into a clear WR2 role with a better quarterback throwing him the ball. Fantasy managers should take a look at what that combination could produce.

Over the past three seasons, it is fair to say no player in fantasy football has been more consistent than Doubs. He has averaged 10.3, 10.2, and 10.3 fantasy points per game. That is not a typo. Three straight years of essentially identical production.

He is useful every season, though more as a player you plug into your lineup in a bind who will not leave you with a zero. Doubs has never been a needle mover, and I am not going to pretend otherwise.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

The reason for that capped ceiling is worth understanding. Doubs spent his entire career mired in the Green Bay receiver rotation, splitting snaps with a rotating cast and never getting a genuine opportunity to break out. Producing at that level while sharing a room that deep is more impressive than the raw numbers suggest.

New England changes the arrangement. He lands behind A.J. Brown, which is a real target hierarchy, but he is the unquestioned WR2 in that building. Although Jordan Love is a talented quarterback, Drake Maye is undeniably an upgrade, and that matters for a receiver whose value hinges on volume and efficiency rather than explosive plays.

The schedule works in his favor too. The Patriots are now playing a first-place schedule, which should force them to throw more often than Doubs was accustomed to in Green Bay. Tougher opponents mean more negative game scripts, and negative game scripts mean pass attempts.

Put those two things together and the math gets interesting. Doubs can very likely maintain the 19.3% target share he posted last season. The difference is that it would now be a share of a considerably larger passing pie. That is exactly how a player at this price outperforms his cost without needing anything dramatic to change about who he is.

His efficiency supports it as well. Doubs posted a 1.85 yards per route run last season, which is meaningfully better than what you typically get from a receiver ranked this far down the board. He wins his matchups. He simply has not been asked to do it often enough.

There is one more wrinkle that makes him more appealing to me than most. I have a bit of a fade on Brown this season, and if Brown falls short of what the market expects, some of that production has to go somewhere. Doubs is the most obvious beneficiary.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

Doubs is my WR49 against a WR52 ADP. I am not sure how much of a ceiling exists here, and I would not draft him expecting one. But I am reasonably confident he outperforms his ADP expectation, and WR3 production is firmly in play.

If you need a safe, reliable set of hands late in drafts, Doubs is worth a look.

title: 'Each monster truck jump has the g-force of a car crash'
description: The father and daughter duo thrill crowds with their exhilarating monster truck stunts.
fullText:
Most fathers and daughters bond over shared activities like camping and hiking but for Georgina and Tony Dixon it is their shared love of monster trucks that brings them together.

Monster trucks have been part of 23-year-old Georgina's life since day one. Her dad bought his first monster truck, Swamp Thing, in 2003 - the year she was born.

Having grown up with the motorsport in Melksham, Wiltshire, Georgina has followed in her dad's footsteps and she is now thought to be the youngest female truck driver in the country.

"About two years ago, I started doing monster trucks full-time and I love it," she said. "It's absolutely amazing."

The pair are due to thrill crowds at Truck Fest South West at the Bath and West Showground in Shepton Mallet this weekend, performing stunts on the legendary Swamp Thing monster truck.

Performing all around the world, they take it in turns to perform arena stunts on the 12ft (3.6m) 4x4 vehicle, such as high-flying jumps, car crushes, slap wheelies and power donuts.

"The best bit for me is meeting all the fans," said Georgina.

"You get so much adrenaline, your hands start shaking as soon as you get out of the truck.

"Each jump in a monster truck has the same sort of g-force as a 30mph (48km) car crash.

"Obviously we have all the safety gear but that's the sort of forces you are expecting when you hit a car in a monster truck."

REPLACE THIS STORY AND ADD INDEX TOP THREE HERE

Tony said he was inspired to own a monster truck as a boy watching television shows about monster trucks in the early 1980s.

"They would have them on Christmas Day specials," he said. "I'd rather watch the monster trucks than unwrap my presents."

Much like her dad, Georgina also loved monster trucks as a child.

In 2023, she officially earned her monster truck driving licence and she has since turned her passion into a full-time job.

Tony described monster truck driving as being "like a quad-bike on steroids".

He said: "It accelerates really, really fast.

"I've got some fast cars but the monster truck accelerates quicker than all the cars," he said.

What makes a monster truck so distinct, he said, was the "massive 66-inch tyres".

Measuring about 5ft (1.5m), the tyres are about the same height as Georgina and getting into the vehicle is not easy.

"The monster truck is made up of all these pipes and tubes and you essentially climb up the side of it because the truck has got no doors to climb in," said Georgina.

Driving a monster truck can also prove to be tricky, she said.

"With a normal car you've got front steering but on this we've got two forms of steering... back steering, which is controlled by a joystick, but, at the same time, you've got to drive the front wheels with a steering wheel.

"So you've got to be good at PlayStation or Xbox."

title: Updated Deebo Samuel Fantasy Outlook 2026: Will He Bounce Back After 49ers Reunion?
description: At the peak of his powers, Deebo Samuel was a fantasy football rockstar. Not only does he have a 1,400-yard season on his resume, but he ran for 16 scores over a three-year stretch and has been remarkably durable for a player who plays with the sort of physicality that he does.
fullText:
At the peak of his powers, Deebo Samuel was a fantasy football rockstar. Not only does he have a 1,400-yard season on his resume, but he ran for 16 scores over a three-year stretch and has been remarkably durable for a player who plays with the sort of physicality that he does.

Back with San Francisco, Samuel is a 30-year-old looking to bounce back. Father Time is a threat, but this is an offense that could use playmakers and has a workhorse running back who is a flight risk.

For a player like this, it's all about role. As you'd expect from a player like this, the YAC skills have regressed a bit and the raw abilities are trending in the wrong direction, but this is an offensive system that is annually one of the most efficient in the league and excels at putting their skill position players in the best spot possible.

With the Commanders last season, Samuel's yards after the catch per reception were 25.3% below his career norm. This system can only repair so much and asking for anything close to peak-Samuel isn't responsible.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

That said, what is stopping him from getting a handful of touches per week?

Rickey Pearsall's 2026 season ended before it started, George Kittle might not be fully deployed until the middle of the season, and if we are worried about the trajectory of Samuel, what are we saying about Mike Evans?

As you can see from my rankings, I'm not high on Samuel and I'm not actively targeting him. That can be true while I still admit that there is a cleaner path to him mattering on a regular basis than some of the other WRs in this tier.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

Betting against Kyle Shanahan is poor practice. Samuel is just two seasons removed from averaging 14.9 yards per catch and hauling in a career-best seven touchdowns. I think this will be an up-and-down season for the veteran and if you can get ahead of the good times, you could extract value in such a way that your team benefits in a major way.

The live blog here starts rolling below at 3 a.m. ET. Come in and say hi!

135 lbs.: Umar Nurmagomedov vs. Song Yadong

115 lbs.: Yan Xiaonan vs. Denise Gomes

135 lbs.: Aoriqileng vs. Kai Asakura

125 lbs.: Sumudaerji def. Alex Perez by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

205 lbs.: Liu Ce def. Levi Rodrigues by KO (right hook), round 1 (4:26) — HIGHLIGHTS

125 lbs.: Bilal Hasan def. Nilson Rojas by KO (straight right), round 2 (2:28) — HIGHLIGHTS

125 lbs.: Andre Lima def. Namsrai Batbayar by submission (guillotine), round 3 (3:03)

125 lbs.: Rei Tsuruya def. Kevin Borjas by submission (rear naked choke), round 1 (4:14)

145 lbs.: Sean Woodson def. Jack Jenkins by split decision (29-28, 28-29, 29-28)

135 lbs.: Francesco Nuzzi def. Xiao Long by TKO (punches), round 1 (1:00)

135 lbs.: Hector Santiago def. Lawrence Lui by KO (punches), round 2 (0:53)

115 lbs.: Julia Polastri def. Jingnan Xiong by KO (headkick), round 1 (3:06)

170 lbs.: Cam Nelson def. Ding Meng by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

Round 1: Just like the first fight, Perez is trying to blitz through Sumudaerji's reach to land punches. And just like the first time, Sumudaerji is able to back up and avoid those. Sumudaerji has landed some hard leg kicks, but nothing upstairs so far. Sumudaerji lands more good low kicks, targeting the lead leg. Perez goes for a desperate takedown. Sumudaerji targets the neck as they go down along the fence. We've got a stalemate now.

Round 2: Perez ducks under a punch and gets an early takedown with lots of time to work. Sumudaerji posts up and stands against the wall. Perez has the bodylock and he takes Sumudaerji for a ride. Sumudaerji gets back up, though. This time he breaks the lock and gets away. Perez gets another takedown, this time away from the fence. Perez lands a little ground and pound. Sumudaerji lands some elbows from the bottom, but this is Perez's round.

Round 3: Perez jumps in on a punch and uses that to disguise a takedown attempt. Sumudaerji gets the underhook and manages to stay up initially. Perez keeps digging for the takedown. Sumudaerji manages to escape. Sumudaerji tries to get something going from range, but it's too many kicks and not enough punches. Perez throws a combo and then level changes for another takedown attempt. Sumudaerji defends on the fence again. Perez gets a single leg. Sumudaerji threatens a front choke, but lets it go. Sumudaerji rolls for a leg and there's a scramble. It ends with Sumudaerji behind Perez, pushing him to the cage. They separate with 30 seconds left. It's anyone's fight. Sumudaerji throws some punches, but Perez pushes for another takedown. Sumudaerji flies at Perez when he hears the clacker. It's a close round… I'll give it Sumudaerji.

Official decision: Sumudaerji def. Alex Perez by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

Round 1: Ce bounces around like a karate fighter. He's much bigger than Rodrigues. Rodrigues lands the first hard shot, though. That has Ce covering up, but he's fine. Rodrigues is a lot more willing to engage at this point. He lands a hard one-two. Ce is just offering leg kicks, but those aren't keeping Rodrigues away from him. Rodrigues catches a kick and puts Ce on the fence. Now they brawl. I think Ce senses some urgency here. He pops Rodrigues' head back with some nice jabs. He then drops Rodrigues with a hook. Rodrigues is up, but he's wobbly. Ce is slow to realize. He misses on a spinning kick. Now he lands some hard punches. Rodrigues covers up on the fence. Ce pours it on, but Rodrigues stays in there. He fires back and gets off the fence. Ce hurts him again and Rodrigues is back on the fence. Rodrigues lands another hard shot, but Ce responds and sleeps Rodrigues! What a round/fight!

HOLY S*** 🤯

Liu Ce with a phone booth KNOCKOUT at #UFCShanghai! pic.twitter.com/EN42Dc4CJL

Official decision: Liu Ce def. Levi Rodrigues by KO (right hook), round 1 (4:26)

Round 1: Hasan looks very lively early on. He looks so much faster than Rojas. He lands a nice body kick that has Rojas hurt. Hasan doesn't rush, though. Rojas is able to recover. Hasan gets a takedown and lands some good ground and pound. Rojas works back to his feet, but catches a knee on the way up. Hasan lands more combos to finish a strong round.

Round 2: Rojas rocks Hasan early with a big punch! Hasan is able to recover quickly, though. Rojas is too tired to really push and capitalize anyway. Moments later Hasan steps in and lands a straight right on Rojas' chin and Rojas goes down like a sack of potatoes. That's a wrap.

AS ADVERTISED 🇮🇩

Bilal Hasan gets the stunning KO in his UFC debut!

[ #UFCShanghai is LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/nSNNVZm2h2

Official decision: Bilal Hasan def. Nilson Rojas by KO (straight right), round 2 (2:28)

Namsrai Batbayar vs. Andre Lima: Batbayar looked very raw in this fight. Lima was able to pick him apart on the feet and stay out of the way of all of Batbayar's very telegraphed power punches and kicks. Lima was cruising in the third and, after Batbayar whiffed on a punch, he jumped the guillotine and used that to take home the victory.

DON'T BE SILLY 🪿@Andremascote jumped the gilly and landed the mounted sub at #UFCShanghai!! pic.twitter.com/yqfiPtRFm6

Official decision: Andre Lima def. Namsrai Batbayar by submission (guillotine), round 3 (3:03)

Rei Tsuruya vs. Kevin Borjas: Tsuruya showed off some incredible aggression in this bout. he launched himself at Borjas off the opening bell, got him down and then pummelled him with ground and pound. Borjas was forced into total defense. After taking a lot of punishment on the ground, Borjas was finally able to get up, but Tsuruya took him down again, took his back and then attacked with the choke. He had Borjas' arm pinned with his leg and once he started to squeeze it was game over.

This man is a problem 😤 @UFC_Rei 

That's back-to-back RD1 submissions for Tsuruya!

[ #UFCShanghai is LIVE NOW on @ParamountPlus ] pic.twitter.com/gNG8DNRBGA

Official decision: Rei Tsuruya def. Kevin Borjas by submission (rear naked choke), round 1 (4:14)

Jack Jenkins vs. Sean Woodson: Jenkins had a lot of trouble with Woodson's size and reach in the first round. In the second he managed to sweep Woodson on the ground and spend a lot of time on top. That set up a pivotal third round. In the third, Jenkins was able to crash through range and land some shots and keep Woodson on the fence. Woodson was able to defend well and land some good single shots. I scored the third for Jenkins, but it was a razor thin round.

Official decision: Sean Woodson def. Jack Jenkins by split decision (29-28, 28-29, 29-28)

Francesco Nuzzi vs. Xiao Long: Long came in hot, flying at Nuzzi with a knee off the opening bell. Nuzzi brushed that off, though. Moments later, Nuzzi caught Long with an eye poke that paused the action. Shortly after the restart Nuzzi caught Long with a hard left and then blitzed him with about a dozen shots that had Long flailing on the canvas. Herb Dean stepped in and called the fight, much to Long's dismay (who then almost stumbled out the cage door).

BERSERKER MODE 🇮🇹💥

Francesco Nuzzi makes good on his UFC debut with a first round TKO at #UFCShanghai!! pic.twitter.com/2TdkVXgD3z

Official decision: Francesco Nuzzi def. Xiao Long by TKO (punches), round 1 (1:00)

Lawrence Lui vs. Hector Santiago: Former kickboxer Santiago showed off his heavy striking in his UFC debut here. He landed on Lui in the first round, but really put his foot on the gas in the second. He rocked Lui with a glancing blow to the head and then stalked him down and dropped him with a straight right to the jaw.

Welcome to the UFC 🙌

Hector Santiago simply couldn't miss on his way to a TKO win at #UFCShanghai! pic.twitter.com/fCB7fmolxC

Official decision: Hector Santiago def. Lawrence Lui by KO (punches), round 2 (0:53)

Jingnan Xiong vs. Julia Polastri: Polastri gave us one of the nastiest women's MMA KOs we've seen in UFC. She threw a two punch combo and then followed that with a head kick. Xiong was leaning back from the punches and moved her head right into the kick. She was out before she hit the ground. Polastri would have won a POTN bonus had she made weight for this.

OH MY GOSH 🤯@Polastri_UFC just gave us an INSANE headkick KO highlight at #UFCShanghai! pic.twitter.com/eUIrYXmdcR

Official decision: Julia Polastri def. Jingnan Xiong by KO (headkick), round 1 (3:06)

Ding Meng vs. Cam Nelson: Nelson made this a boring fight and that was bad for Ding and the crowd in Shanghai. Ding had the striking advantage, but his total lack of takedown defense ruined this fight for him. Nelson took him down with ease in the first two rounds. Nelson got tired in the third, but Ding wasn't able to take advantage of that.

Official decision: Cam Nelson def. Ding Meng by unanimous decision (29-28, 29-28, 29-28)

title: Updated Rashid Shaheed Fantasy Outlook 2026: Is the Seahawks WR a Late-Round Target?
description: Rashid Shaheed arrived in Seattle midway through last season and essentially vanished from fantasy relevance. His numbers with the Seahawks were about as bad as they get for a starting-caliber receiver.
fullText:
Rashid Shaheed arrived in Seattle midway through last season and essentially vanished from fantasy relevance. His numbers with the Seahawks were about as bad as they get for a starting-caliber receiver. Reports this offseason suggest there was more going on than a simple talent problem. Should fantasy managers take a shot on Shaheed in 2026?

When I first started preparing for the upcoming season, Shaheed was an easy fade.

After joining the Seahawks last year, his receiving role cratered completely. He went from a legitimate weekly WR3 in New Orleans to waiver wire fodder. Shaheed averaged a mere 2.8 targets per game in Seattle and did not score a single offensive touchdown. His receiving yardage collapsed from 50.9 per game with the Saints all the way down to 20.9 with the Seahawks.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

No role. No production. I was out.

But the more I sat with it, the more I started warming up to him. Seattle does not have a clear WR2 behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba, and Shaheed is a legitimately talented player. Those two facts sitting next to each other are hard to ignore.

I rarely like making excuses for players. In this case, the argument that Shaheed simply did not have time to be integrated into the offense holds real water. Learning a new playbook midseason is genuinely difficult, and there have been reports this offseason confirming that is exactly what happened. The expectation now is that a bigger role is coming after a full offseason to absorb the system.

The situation supports it as well. Seattle projects as one of the better offenses in the league, and they are the defending Super Bowl champions. There are worse places to be the second option in a passing game.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

It also does not hurt that Shaheed is likely to chip in a special teams touchdown or two along the way. That is free production most receivers at this price cannot offer, and it can single-handedly rescue a week.

Shaheed is my WR54 against a WR56 ADP, which tells you this is not a strong disagreement with the market. He is essentially free in drafts. At that cost, I am perfectly fine swinging on the WR3 upside he possesses.

title: Updated Rashod Bateman Fantasy Outlook 2026: Is the Ravens WR a Late-Round Dart Throw?
description: Rashod Bateman enters 2026 trapped in a low-volume passing offense with significant target competition and a capped ceiling. Fantasy football managers should avoid drafting him and focus their investments on the elite pieces of the Baltimore roster.
fullText:
Rashod Bateman enters 2026 trapped in a low-volume passing offense with significant target competition and a capped ceiling. Fantasy football managers should avoid drafting him and focus their investments on the elite pieces of the Baltimore roster.

The historical data regarding the Baltimore offense paints a concerning picture for Bateman. Lamar Jackson has never supported a secondary wide receiver who posted top 40 PPR numbers and with Zay Flowers' star continuing to ascend, I'm not sure that trend changes.

Even with the transition to Declan Doyle on the coaching staff, there is no guarantee that this offense looks dramatically different given the way the roster is built. If the offense does evolve to support a second receiver, Ja'Kobi Lane has been turning heads throughout the summer and could easily step into that role instead of Bateman: now you're layering risk on a thin bet to begin with.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

The structural design of the offense further limits opportunities for fringe pass catchers. This is a run-centric team where Mark Andrews and Derrick Henry soak up all sorts of touchdown equity. Neither Andrews nor Henry will record receptions in bulk, but both players score with regularity, that much we know.

Given the heavy reliance on the ground game and the concentrated scoring distribution, it is hard to imagine Bateman recording enough target volume to truly matter on a consistent basis.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

That reality does not mean Bateman will fail to produce any usable weeks. There almost certainly will be spikes in production because those outlier games always happen during an NFL season. The problem is predicting when those usable weeks will occur and I'd rather not play that game.

Your strategy should be simple when it comes to this AFC contender. You should spend up to acquire the elite options in this offense or avoid the unit entirely. Jackson, Henry, and Flowers are all fully capable of leading your fantasy team. The ancillary options like Bateman, however, remain significant underdogs to remain rostered for the entire season.

title: Updated Denzel Boston Fantasy Outlook 2026: Should Managers Stash the Browns WR?
description: Denzel Boston enters the NFL as an intriguing rookie with a promising long-term trajectory but immediate limitations. Fantasy football managers should view him as a developmental stash rather than an early-season contributor in redraft formats, and maybe a DFS target should things break in his favor as the leaves turn.
fullText:
Denzel Boston enters the NFL as an intriguing rookie with a promising long-term trajectory but immediate limitations. Fantasy football managers should view him as a developmental stash rather than an early-season contributor in redraft formats, and maybe a DFS target should things break in his favor as the leaves turn.

The Browns invested significant draft capital in Boston, and that's always a good thing (39th overall pick). He earned that premium draft position after an explosive final collegiate season at Washington where his yards per catch increased to 14.2. He also found the end zone 11 times on just 62 receptions, a skill that can very much pay the fantasy bills should it carry over.

Managers must factor in a steep learning curve and the environment that is working against him. While Boston's frame created mismatches in college, his size will not be as overwhelming against professional defensive backs, and that naturally will take some skill development.

START PREPARING: PFN's FREE Fantasy Draft Simulator

And then you have the quarterback situation in Cleveland, both short-and-long term. Shedeur Sanders proved underwhelming last season, and that left the door open for Deshaun Watson, who the city and fans actively dislike, to win the starting gig this summer.

Because of these quarterback constraints, Boston requires extreme patience from managers. Boston possesses the superior long-term upside for dynasty leagues over KC Concepcion, in my eyes, because his size is something that can't be learned. Yet, his counterpart represents the better short-term fantasy bet because he offers a slippery skill set that translates in a much cleaner way to the current quarterback limitations.

FANTASY RANKINGS: PFN's FREE Fantasy PPR, Half-PPR, and Non-PPR Rankings

Boston relies more on vertical development, and that puts him at the mercy of the man getting him the ball. Cleveland currently lacks that in a major way, and I don't see much in the way of positive signals. Draft Boston in dynasty formats for his physical profile, but leave him on the wire in standard redraft leagues.

title: ‘Enes Kanter Stats’ — Sophie Cunningham’s Rough Night Vs. Sun Sees WNBA Fans Question Audacity of Fever Star’s 6th Player of the Year Case
description: Sophie Cunningham has dominated nationwide headlines for over a month following her comments against trans athletes’ eligibility in women’s sports. On Friday night, it was her play on the hardwood that caught basketball fans’ attention.
fullText:
Sophie Cunningham has dominated nationwide headlines for over a month following her comments against trans athletes' eligibility in women's sports.

On Friday night, it was her play on the hardwood that caught basketball fans' attention. In a comfortable, 20-point win over the Connecticut Sun, Cunningham registered a single point off the bench, and fans weren't all too pleased with her performance, to say the least.

In 14 minutes of play, Cunningham dropped 1 point on 0-3 shooting from the field, along with 3 turnovers. Her single offensive contribution came from the charity stripe, and most of her damage was on the defensive end of the floor.

The WNBA world was livid as they expected more from a 'Sixth Player of the Year' candidate.

"Sophie Cunningham scored 1 point in 14 minutes for the Fever tonight. Thought I'd share these stats, since she wants us to talk about basketball now," said one user, who has been sharing her stats on X each time she underperforms.

This post alluded toCunningham's comments on August 5, "I'm going to let people just do the speaking for themselves, but for me, I want to get back to basketball. It's always been about basketball."

Another X user, whileroasting her for her 1-point stat line, wrote, "If only this grifter could hit buckets as well as point fingers. She sucks."

One WNBA observer pointed out that merely a day ago, the Fever created multiple posts to campaign for Cunningham to win the 'Sixth Player of the Year' award.

They wrote, "And the Fever has the nerve to create a 6POY for her," which was followed by numerous crying laughing emojis.

Another kept it simple and wrote, "Enes Kanter stats," alluding to the fact that Kanter, who has also been in headlines since his WNBA Draft declaration, was never a star during his 11-year NBA stint.

Last night's game saw the Fever lead by 15 points at the end of the first half. It was never truly close as Indy ran away with the 111-91 win.

So, it wasn't incumbent upon Cunningham to have a double-digit scoring night and shoot her usual, 44%+ blistering percentage from beyond the arc.

DON'T MISS: 'We Need More of This,' 'Clown' – After Enes Kanter, WNBA World Split Over Royce White's 'UNREAL COURTSIDE ANTICS' at Fever-Sun Game

However, with the Fever making it very clear they want her to win an award for her bench role, scoring a single point certainly didn't move the needle in her favor.

In fact, the current frontrunner for the 'Sixth Player of the Year' award is the Golden State Valkyries' Janelle Salaün, who is averaging 12.9 points on 42.5% shooting from the field while holding her own on both ends of the floor against opposing bench units.

The Valkyries also hold a better record than the Fever in the standings (28-11 vs. 26-14).

With merely four games left for the Fever to play in this regular season, she would have to make quite the impression to make people forget about her 1-point performance and try to dethrone Salaün as the favorite for the award.

This article originally appeared on Pro Football Network.

title: Cleveland Browns 53-man roster cuts tracker
description: Tracking the Browns trimming the roster to 53 before Sunday’s 6:00 PM deadline.
fullText:
The Cleveland Browns have until Sunday at 6:00 PM ET to make roster cuts and announce their initial 53-man roster. Some of those cuts or rumors about roster moves might leak early, though. The Browns may also announce them in waves — for example, some cuts may be announced Friday, some on Saturday, etc.

All players who are released with less than four years of service must go through waivers and are eligible to be claimed by any other team until 1:00 PM ET on Monday. After that, any unclaimed player can be signed and teams will begin to fill out their 16-man practice squads.

Veterans with more than four years of service can sign immediately after being released.

You can also use the comments section to discuss cuts around the NFL that may be of interest to Cleveland. According to FanDuel, the Browns are 225/1 odds to win the Super Bowl, heading into final roster cuts.

7:30 AM: Reminder that the Browns are scheduled to practice today, with players speaking to the media at 11 AM, with Todd Monken following at 11:50 before the 12:15 practice. It would be somewhat strange, unless there was some secret plan with a player or two, for more than 53 players to be practicing today. Then again, Monken can do what he wants until the players are cut. Would also be risking injuries for players who are going to get cut and could sign elsewhere. Just seems unlikely, so stayed tuned here to the tracker all morning!

3:36 PM: By my count, the Browns are now down to 73 players, meaning they have 20 moves remaining to get down to 53 players by Sunday at 6:00 pm ET. I'm not sure if there will be any more moves today, but my current guess is that the remaining moves will be announced tomorrow. What you might start hearing, before that official news release, are players' agents leaking that "so-and-so has been informed that they have made the 53-man roster," or some sources indicating that a particular player has been notified that they'll be cut.

Going back to the first batch of cuts below, none of them are a surprise. Avery was a guy on my 53-man roster, but he was meant to be a temporary placeholder due to injury concerns; I did not expect him to be a long-term player on the roster.

3:25 PM: We have our first batch of Browns cuts: 16 moves in total (4 contracts terminated, 12 players waived).

The terminated players are TE Jack Stoll (from IR), OT Tyre Phillips, CB Tre Avery, and CB Tyler Hall.

The players waived are WR Ben Patterson, TE Jermaine Terry II, TE Drew Biber, OT Jeremiah Byers, OT Izavion Miller, DT Coziah Izzard, DT Patrick Jenkins, DE Jamil Muhammad, CB Jeremiah McClendon, CB Nate Evans, S Christopher Edmonds, and P Nik Constantinou.

1:24 PM: Not a reportable rumor as I don't have a second source, but enough to at least share here as a keep-your-eyes-out kinda thing. I've heard that the Falcons and Chargers at least discussed a Tua trade, which could open up a spot for Dillon Gabriel in Atlanta (just as everyone joked/expected when Kevin Stefanski was hired there). – Jared

10:15 AM: Regarding the timing of the Browns' roster cuts, Jared Mueller made a good point on one of our site's internal communications. Head coach Todd Monken is scheduled to talk to the media at 11:00 AM ET on Saturday, with practice to follow at 12:15 PM on Saturday.

It seems highly likely that the Browns will have their 53-man roster decided by then. I've never heard of a case where the team keeps players around for one more practice in between making their final roster cuts.

10:02 AM: Good morning, everyone! I posted my 53-man roster projection this morning. There were plenty of tough decisions at quarterback, wide receiver, tight end, and cornerback. With these potential roster cuts, news could literally hit any time between now and Sunday evening. Typically, Andrew Berry does not wait through the deadline to make cuts. We'll keep you posted on any Browns-related news that comes in, as well as other cuts around the league.

One thing to keep in mind is that the final preseason games in general takes place today, as only a few games took place Thursday evening. In general, you likely won't see league-wide news about roster cuts until Saturday.

12:00 AM: The Browns just finished their third and final preseason game, beating the New England Patriots by a score of 37-13. We already heard about one big roster cut on Thursday morning, as reports indicated that Cleveland was waiving WR Cedric Tillman. Tillman was going to be a cut on my 53-man roster projection anyway, due to the way things have unfolded in camp this year and the impressive nature of rookies KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston.

title: Penix Closes Gap as Falcons QB Race Boils Over
description: The gap Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa has been closed in the Atlanta Falcons quarterback race, according to Yahoo Sports . NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport says the lead Tagovailoa held is gone. Both players will now split first-team reps to settle the starting job. The competition is wide open and the pressure is…
fullText:
The gap Michael Penix Jr. and Tua Tagovailoa has been closed in the Atlanta Falcons quarterback race, according to Yahoo Sports. NFL Network insider Ian Rapoport says the lead Tagovailoa held is gone. Both players will now split first-team reps to settle the starting job. The competition is wide open and the pressure is on for both men.

Tagovailoa started with a huge advantage. He looked great during the offseason while Penix was stuck on the sideline. The organization wanted him to win the job and move forward as the starter. That plan relied on Penix staying injured for a while. But the knee injury healed faster than expected.

Penix needed surgery in the week of November 24, 2025, to address a partially torn ACL in his left knee. Before that hurt knee, he threw for 1,982 yards. He completed 60.1 per cent of his passes. Nine total touchdowns and three interceptions were recorded by him during the 2025 season. Now he is back and ready to fight.

Tagovailoa has not looked as sharp in the preseason. Both in practice and in games, Rapoport noted that he had been inconsistent. The gap that seemed so wide has shrunk to nothing. Rapoport explained that Tagovailoa 'had a big-time lead in this race'. That lead is under serious pressure now.

Falcons head coach Kevin Stefanski confirmed the split reps. This move proves the door is open for Penix. Rapoport stated that while he seems to have been practicing better the last couple of days, the door is open for Michael Penix. That quote from Rapoport sums up the whole situation perfectly.

The coach made the call after Penix was cleared for 11-on-11 work. This means the competition can now properly begin. Both players get to show what they can do on the field. No more waiting for the injured guy to catch up. They are both in the mix right now.

Penix knows what he can do. He told reporters that as far as a pocket, he can do everything. He is confident in his skills. The only thing holding him back is his doctor's advice on taking hits. His doctor is still waiting for the point when he is comfortable with him taking hits.

That time is getting closer every day. The Falcons' quarterback decision could soon become much clearer. Fans will see the real difference between these two soon enough. The split reps are the first step in a long battle.

There is plenty at stake for Tagovailoa. He is on a one-year deal. This game could be his only chance to prove he belongs. If he loses the job, he might not have another shot in Atlanta. He needs to show he is the long-term starter in the NFL.

Penix faces his own pressure too. He spent much of training camp working his way back. He cannot afford to waste this opportunity. He needs to reclaim the starting role he appeared set to compete for before his injury. The clock is ticking for both of them.

The original plan was for Penix to rehab his knee and return when healthy. The team hoped he would just give Atlanta another option if a change was needed during the season. Now that plan is dead. The team has to pick one man to lead the offense.

Tagovailoa has struggled during the preseason. Rapoport noted that he had been inconsistent both in practice and in games. The door is open for Michael Penix to walk right in. The Falcons fans will get their answer very soon. The race has reached a boiling point.

title: Forest to bid £40m for Everton teenager Armstrong
description: Nottingham Forest launch an ambitious bid to sign Everton's teenage midfielder Harrison Armstrong.
fullText:
Nottingham Forest have launched an ambitious bid to sign Everton's teenage midfielder Harrison Armstrong.

Forest are keen to strengthen before the end of the transfer window and, as reported by The Athletic, are preparing to offer £40m plus a potential sell-on clause to clinch a deal for Armstrong.

It would be a major surprise should Everton sanction a deal, but there is hope at Forest that they can pull off the move to prise away the elegant England under-19 star, who is regarded as having a big future ahead of him.

Armstrong, 19, has made 23 appearances for Everton and started in their 2-0 Premier League win against Crystal Palace last week.

As yet, there are no indications as to whether Everton will agree to sell.

The Friedkin Group, Everton's American owners, will be risking the fury of their own fanbase should they agree to the sale of Harrison Armstrong to Nottingham Forest.

The notion that Everton could even consider parting with Armstrong sparked an instant reaction of disbelief and anger among supporters, with the teenager regarded as their brightest home-grown prospect for years and a big hope for the future.

As yet, there are no indications that Everton will accept an offer, but Forest's interest is real, although it would be a real coup should they pull it off.

It would also send out worrying signals about the scale of TFG's ambitions.

Manager David Moyes has been frustrated by the club's lack of incoming transfer activity this summer.

Moyes made it abundantly clear after Wednesday's 4-0 Carabao Cup second-round win at Championship side Preston that he wanted reinforcements.

His hope was that TFG would provide backing for further arrivals.

Since then, however, Everton's main creator Iliman Ndiaye has been heavily linked with Manchester City, and now Forest are ready to test their resolve over Armstrong.

How Moyes would view, or indeed explain, such a sale, would be intriguing. It would appear totally at odds with his stated intention of building a better squad.

And while Everton and their support may have to accept their prize assets being spirited away by clubs such as Manchester City, the idea that their most promising young player could be taken away by Nottingham Forest – a club they would be expecting to challenge or even surpass – may be harder to stomach.

That is why the manner in which Everton handle Forest's approach for Armstrong, who has already excelled this season, may be a defining moment for TFG and Moyes.

title: USC countdown to kickoff: Recalling Trojans DL Korey Foreman
description: Today, we conclude our countdown by looking at a defensive lineman who made perhaps the biggest play of the Lincoln Riley era to date
fullText:
Countdown to kickoff is back! USC will kick off its 2026 football season on August 29 when the Trojans host San Jose State at the Coliseum. In this series, we will be counting down the days until the season opener by highlighting a notable Trojan who wore each number.

Our countdown has finally reached its conclusion! With zero days to go, today we look at former USC defensive lineman Korey Foreman.

Career highlights: In 2021, the Trojans made headlines when they landed Foreman, who was the No. 1 overall recruit in the country. However, he never quite lived up to the hype that surrounded him at USC, recording just 14 total tackles and 2.5 sacks in three years with the Trojans.

Foreman did make one massive play during his time in Cardinal and Gold, however. In 2022, No. 7 USC led No. 16 UCLA 48-45, but the Bruins had the ball and were driving late for a potential game-tying or game-winning score. However, Foreman intercepted a pass from UCLA quarterback Dorian Thompson-Robinson, sealing the game. The victory brought the Victory Bell back to USC, clinched a double-digit win season for the Trojans, and sent them to the Pac-12 Championship Game.

After USC: Following the 2023 season, Foreman elected to enter the transfer portal, landing at Fresno State. In two years with the Bulldogs, he recorded 45 tackles, six sacks, three forced fumbles, and five passes defended.

After going undrafted in the 2026 NFL Draft, Foreman attended rookie minicamp with both the New England Patriots and Tampa Bay Buccaneers.
