title: Klint Kubiak’s recent comments suggest Aidan O’Connell closer to starters role over Fernando Mendoza
description: Fernando Mendoza could be listed as the Raiders' third-string quarterback.Fernando Mendoza’s journey to becoming the starting quarterback of the Las Vegas Raiders might take longer than expected. Raiders head coach...
fullText:
Fernando Mendoza's journey to becoming the starting quarterback of the Las Vegas Raiders might take longer than expected.

Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak has not revealed who will be their starting quarterback, despite expectations leading to Kirk Cousins. Michael David Smith of NBC Sports reported that Kubiak was asked on Friday about the backup spot and said a decision hasn't been made.

"We've got three guys that are ready to play," Kubiak told Smith. "It's going to be some hard decisions on who's 1, who's 2. That's not a decision we have to make today, but those are discussions that are ongoing."

Throughout the offseason, the expectation for Mendoza has been he will be Cousins' backup this season, as the veteran quarterback has been mentoring the rookie since he was selected with the No.1 overall pick of the NFL Draft this past April.

But given the rookie's early struggles in the preseason, it could suggest that veteran quarterback Aidan O'Connell could have the upper edge over him in the quarterback battle.

O'Connell has experienced life as a starter in the NFL before and has outperformed Mendoza in the preseason.

But even with history on the veteran's side, the present time suggests O'Connell could win the backup spot. Mostly because he hasn't turned the ball over.

Mendoza has also shown his struggles under pressure, as he's been sacked four times, while O'Connell has only taken 1.

title: Cavaliers Get Bad News as Franchise Superstar Expected to Request a Trade
description: Not too long ago, crickets could be heard in Cleveland. Then the Cavaliers shook awake, making multiple trades and locking in their superstar point guard for another three years. The Cavs have plenty to look forward to entering the 2026-27 season especially after landing Peyton Watson, the 23-year-old former Denver Nuggets star who has future […] The post Cavaliers Get Bad News as Franchise Superstar Expected to Request a Trade appeared first on HEAVY.
fullText:
Not too long ago, crickets could be heard in Cleveland. Then the Cavaliers shook awake, making multiple trades and locking in their superstar point guard for another three years.

The Cavs have plenty to look forward to entering the 2026-27 season especially after landing Peyton Watson, the 23-year-old former Denver Nuggets star who has future superstar written all over him.

Watson should give the Cavs what they lacked in previous seasons — an athletic wing who can score on one end and play lockdown defense on the other.

Of course, like with any franchise, there will be long-term questions surrounding superstars Donovan Mitchell and James Harden, each of whom are at the stage of their careers where it is all about winning at the highest level, though Mitchell, 29, is considerably younger than Harden.

Suddenly, there has been plenty to celebrate this offseason for the Cavs … until ESPN dropped its annual Summer Forecast, where a panel of experts weighed in on some of the NBA's biggest questions. Then there was the question of which superstar is most likely to request a trade next.

Harden made that list, receiving the fifth most votes among stars Anthony Davis (1), Kyrie Irving (2), Kevin Durant (T-3), Zion Williamson (T-3) and Jaylen Brown (T-5).

Of course, Harden just signed a three-year contract worth roughly $97 million. Even at 37, the Cavs are ready to commit to their 11-time All-Star at least until he reaches age 40.

Then again, it is not like Harden, one of the greatest offensive engines the NBA has seen, is a stranger to changing teams. In fact, the Cavs, who traded for Harden ahead of last season's trade deadline, are the former league MVP's fifth team in the last five years. That is hard to ignore.

It is fair to say acquiring Harden was a rather ambitious decision by the Cleveland front office. After all, trading the 26-year-old Darius Garland, who has been an All-Star, for a player who is roughly (count 'em) 12 years older and supposedly past his prime is extremely bold.

But the Cavs saw something in Harden that they believed they needed to get over the hump in the East. And apparently, they still believe that way, as Cleveland.com recently noted.

"The Cleveland Cavaliers have officially signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million fully guaranteed deal, which includes a third-year player option and a 15% trade kicker," an article in Cleveland.com read. "While the annual salary is slightly higher than initially expected for the soon-to-be 37-year-old, it serves as a reward for his willingness to be financially flexible throughout the summer. The structure of this agreement — taking less money upfront — was vital in helping the Cavaliers afford other key roster additions under the salary cap. Beyond the financials, Harden addresses a critical on-court vulnerability. He provides essential offensive stability, elite playmaking capability when Donovan Mitchell is resting, and potentially the playmaking key to fully unlocking Evan Mobley's offensive development over the next few seasons."

Harden showed his chops after landing in Cleveland. The former All-Star averaged nearly 21 points and eight assists per game and shot close to 43 percent from the 3-point line for the Cavs in the regular season.

The Cavs will need a lot more of that next season, especially in a revamped Eastern Conference.

title: Nets' Egor Demin doesn't make HoopsHype's top-27 shooting guard list

fullText:
Brooklyn Nets guard Egor Demin had a solid rookie season where he showed his ability to shoot the three-pointer better than anyone, except the Nets' coaching staff, anticipated coming into last year. title: Abbey Mastracco: Mets giving fans a reason to show up in a bad season
description: NEW YORK — They say misery loves company, and in the midst of a miserable Mets season, the team found a creative way to bring fans together: A singles night at the ballpark. The event, put together by Hot and Single, an Instagram dating series created by Liv Schreiber, brought people from around the area looking for love, friendship or just their next ex-situationship to Citi Field earlier ...
fullText:
NEW YORK — They say misery loves company, and in the midst of a miserable Mets season, the team found a creative way to bring fans together: A singles night at the ballpark. The event, put together by Hot and Single, an Instagram dating series created by Liv Schreiber, brought people from around the area looking for love, friendship or just their next ex-situationship to Citi Field earlier this week.

While it's too early to know if Singles Night produced any lasting love connections, we do know the Mets are giving fans reasons to come to the ballpark this season. The product on the field hasn't been what fans expected in 2026, but it hasn't been what the team expected either. The team could have just had a few cheap beer nights and a dollar hot dog night and called it a year, but that's not what the Mets did.

They offered the fans more than baseball. After all, this is supposed to be fun.

Last month, the club announced that tickets for all remaining home games would come with a $10 voucher that could be used for food, beverages or team merchandise. This applied to advance-purchased tickets as well. When you add it all up, the Mets are essentially giving away over $10 million to fans.

Sure, it's tough to get a full meal for $10, but it's a tremendous gesture that has enticed fans who may otherwise feel like it's not worth the effort to watch a losing team.

Going to a baseball game is about more than the game on the field. Teams have increasingly invested in the "experience" of the game. The purists would disagree with this trend, but it might be working in the Mets' favor this season.

The team has been out of contention practically since the season started. The team fired once-popular manager Carlos Mendoza in June. Numerous stars were injured, and the play on the field for much of the year has been anything but enjoyable to watch. Sloppy, listless, uninspired and fundamentally poor. A fan base that is quick to anoint the last guys on the bench as heroes, but just as quick to turn on them, had every reason to turn on the team.

But they didn't turn on Citi Field.

The concession offerings regularly top the lists of best ballpark foods and the giveaways are quality. Personally, I think they've leaned too heavily into gimmicks with newer additions like the Queens Crew dance group and the Five Borough Mascot Race, but feedback has been positive. Seeing Mr. Met walking on his hands in the middle of dancers on top of the dugout while the team is losing big feels like a fever dream. However, the way I've seen kids light up when the mascots take off around the warning track tells me all I need to know.

An Irish band on the concourse for Irish Heritage Night, the wives and girlfriends of the players choosing songs for Women's Appreciation Night — these are details that make games enjoyable and create bonds with the team, whether they're winning or losing.

Ultimately, fans want to see the Mets win, maybe even more than they'd like to meet the love of their life at a game. The product on the field has been far more enjoyable as of late, giving fans even more of a reason to attend games and use those $10 vouchers. So the Mets have gone all in on this scrappy group of journeymen relievers and star smashers.

Love him or not, left-hander Jefry Yan has brought fans to Citi Field. There is tremendous intrigue around the 30-year-old reliever who celebrates strikeouts with wild jumps off the mound and throws 102 from the left side. He's won over his teammates with his energy and enthusiasm.

The rookie outfield duo of Carson Benge and A.J. Ewing have attracted fans who want to see them scale walls to rob home runs. Rookie starter Nolan McLean is dominating hitters with his array of spinning pitches, and rising young starters Christian Scott and Zac Thornton have quickly captured the fan base's heart.

When Kodai Senga changed his warm-up song to Michael Jackson's "Beat It," the team created a theatrical entrance for him that rivals Edwin Diaz's trumpeted entrance. If he excels in a leverage relief role next season, they may be able to sell red "Ghost Fork" jackets in the team store.

The atmosphere at Citi Field has been noticeably more raucous. Interim manager Andy Green has mentioned it on a few occasions, as have members of the team. When you give fans something to cheer for, they'll give it all they have.

The baseball operations group that puts the team together is small compared to the rest of the club's staff. The groups dedicated to selling tickets and sponsorships, and the groups who are tasked with finding new ways to get people to attend baseball games, have excelled in the face of adversity this season.

Sometimes, love in a hopeless place is worth the price of admission.

title: Lester Martinez defends undefeated record and interim title on Saturday against Luka Plantic's power
description: Lester Martinez defends his WBC interim title against unbeaten Luka Plantic on Saturday, with a shot at the Canelo-Mbilli winner waiting for whoever comes out on top.
fullText:
LOS ANGELES — Two undefeated records are on the line Saturday night at the Galen Center.

Lester Martinez (20-0-1, 16 KOs) defends his WBC interim super middleweight title for the first time against Croatia's Luka "The Thunder" Plantic (13-0, 10 KOs), live on ProBox TV. The Guatemalan star climbed into the interim seat in March with a unanimous decision over Immanuwel Aleem, a fight closer than his record suggests it should have been. Plantic, ranked No. 3 by the WBC, arrives unbeaten and unbothered, carrying four defenses of his WBC International title and a finish over previously undefeated Shadiri Musa Bwogi as his calling card.

Both fighters made weight Friday, Martinez at 167.2 pounds and Plantic at 167, and the two stood face to face at the ceremonial weigh-in with nothing left to settle but the fight itself. It's official: this one goes Saturday at the Galen Center.

Martinez and Plantic face off after both fighters made weight Friday.

This is Martinez's biggest stage yet. The move up from the 4,000-seat NOS Events Center in San Bernardino to the 12,000-capacity Galen Center wasn't a scheduling accident. It's what happens when a promoter bets on a fighter's pull, and Martinez has been pulling. "There's no doubt the title is staying in Guatemala," he said at the June kickoff press conference. "I'm gonna continue being the world champion. That I can assure you."

The bigger story sits one fight ahead. Christian Mbilli holds the full WBC title and squares off with Canelo Alvarez in October, and Martinez has made no secret of where his eyes are. "Of course, I'm going to be looking at this fight coming up with Canelo and Mbilli," he said. "Right now, my immediate focus is on Luka and taking care of business on August 29, defending my title. Then we can look forward to that tremendous fight and hope that we fight the winner."

Beat Plantic, and Martinez plants himself first in line for whoever comes out of that superfight. That's the kind of opportunity that turns a rising name into a made one.

Plantic isn't interested in being a stepping stone. The 29-year-old Olympian-turned-pro has built his career on the other side of the Atlantic, and this is the first time the level of opposition matches his ambition. He's not hiding from the moment. "I will take the belt back to Croatia," he said in a recent interview. "One punch can change anything in boxing. I have Croatian power in me. He is good, but I will win." At the June presser, he framed it plainly: "This is a 50/50 fight... we are going to change Guatemala night to Croatia night."

Stylistically, this is pressure against power. Martinez works behind volume and a deep, well-schooled amateur pedigree, but Aleem proved he can be extended and tested over twelve rounds. Plantic hits with more thump on paper and has stopped nine of his last ten opponents, but he's never shared a ring with anyone who moves and works like Martinez does. Whoever solves the other's problem first likely walks away with the belt.

There's a name attached to Martinez's camp that raises the stakes further. His trainer, Brian "BoMac" McIntyre, is the same man who guided Terence Crawford to pound-for-pound status, and Crawford himself has been in with Martinez preparing for this fight. "It feels so good that even though Crawford's retired, he comes to help me and sparred me," Martinez said. "That's such a big, positive name and such a great person, a champion. It feels great to have him help me." That's the caliber of company Martinez is keeping as he angles for a Canelo-tier fight of his own.

Saturday isn't just a title defense. It's Martinez trying to keep his name on the shortest possible list for boxing's biggest fight, and Plantic trying to prove Los Angeles is exactly where his breakout happens.

title: Phillies 1980 World Series Champion Reportedly Dies On Fishing Trip
description: Former Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Larry Christenson has reportedly died at 72
fullText:
Former Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Larry Christenson has died at 72, according to MLB insider Bob Nightengale.

RIP

RIP former Philadelphia Phillies pitcher Larry Christenson, 72, who died unexpectedly this morning while on a fishing trip with family and friends in Washington.

Christenson was a first-round pick by the Phillies in the 1972 MLB Draft. He was the third overall selection out of Maryville High School. By 1973, he had already made his MLB debut. Until 1975, he was up and down between the big leagues and minor leagues, but in 1975 he made 26 starts for the big-league club.

He spent his entire career playing for the Phillies, helping the team win the 1980 World Series as well. He made 220 career starts for the team, posting a 3.79 career ERA. While he made his biggest impact on the mound, he was not too shabby a hitter. He is tied with Rick Wise for the most home runs by a pitcher in Phillies history.

He was a key member of the Phillies rotation when they won three consecutive division titles from 1976 to 1978. He was the team's Game 1 starter in the 1978 National League Championship Series.

After 1978, injuries began to plague his career, but he continued to pitch for the Phillies. He did not have the best performance in the 1980 World Series, exiting Game 1 after recording just one out in the first inning. Still, he is regarded as an important part of the Phillies' World Series-winning team.

title: ‘That’s What Keeping Me Up at Night’ — NFL Analyst Sounds Alarm on Commanders’ Future Ahead of 2026 Season
description: From four wins to the NFC Championship Game was one of the most remarkable turnarounds in recent NFL history. But the Washington Commanders have suffered a hard reset since a thrilling rookie season for Jayden Daniels.
fullText:
From four wins to the NFC Championship Game was one of the most remarkable turnarounds in recent NFL history. But the Washington Commanders have suffered a hard reset since a thrilling rookie season for Jayden Daniels.

After a disastrous 2025 campaign, the team had to hope for a bounce back this season. But the summer has been far from perfect, leaving a few analysts worried about how the team will fare this year.

Last season, with Daniels playing in just seven games, the team quickly fell apart, with an eight-game losing streak effectively ending their year before it even truly began. As a result, they finished with a 5-12 record.

The defense, which ranked second-to-last on PFN's Defense Impact Metric, and the offensive line, which ranked 19th on PFN's Team Offensive Line Impact Metrics, were among the biggest problems for the Commanders last season.

Robert Mays, appearing on "The Athletic Football Show," is incredibly worried that the team hasn't done enough to address those problems. As a result, the fear that this season could completely go to waste is starting to mount as Week 1 draws nearer.

START PREPARING: PFN's Free Fantasy Draft Simulator

"What's keeping me up at night, part of this is, this team just feels to me like it could be a ghost ship," Mays said. "Like, we're just sitting there in Week 7, and we're just riding this thing out over the course of the year; it's like, we're done. We've played out this string; they just don't have it."

Going a step further, he believed that could lead to a complete teardown of the roster: "The misdrafts and the fact that there's just not that underlying level of talent on this team, where we are just in a place where it's time to hit the reset button. That's what's keeping me up at night. That doesn't feel like a remote, far-off possibility."

For a team that looked like a potential perennial contender in the NFC, the turnaround for the Commanders has been bizarre.

Figuring out a quarterback is typically the hardest part of the process for any franchise in the NFL. After what many considered the greatest rookie quarterback season of all-time, it looked like Washington had already found its guy in Daniels. Somehow, it still hasn't been enough for the team, where fans are actively considering what the next phase of the franchise can be.

title: Houston Rockets jersey history No. 30 - Jim Davis (1967-71)
description: During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Davis wore only jersey No. 30 and put up 5.2 points and 3.7 rebounds per game.
fullText:
The Houston Rockets have had players donning a total of 52 different jersey numbers (and have one not part of any numerical series for Houston assistant coach and general manager Carroll Dawson) since their founding at the start of the 1967-68 season, worn by just under 500 players in the course of Rockets history.

To honor all of the players who wore those numbers over the decades, Rockets Wire is covering the entire history of jersey numbers and the players who wore them since the founding of the team all those years ago right up to the present day.

With seven of those jerseys now retired to honor some of the greatest Rockets of all time to wear those jerseys, there is a lot of history to cover.

And for today's article, we will continue with the third of 15 who wore the No. 30, Jim Davis. After ending his college career at Colorado, Davis was picked up with the 29th overall selection of the 1964 NBA Draft by the Detroit Pistons.

The Muncie, Indiana native played the first 3 seasons of his pro career in another league, signing with the (then) St. Louis (now, Atlanta) Hawks in 1967. That ended with a trade to the Houston Rockets in 1971. His stay with the team lasted until he was dealt to Detroit that winter.

During his time suiting up for the Rockets, Davis wore only jersey No. 30 and put up 5.2 points and 3.7 rebounds per game.

All stats and data courtesy of Basketball Reference.

title: Former Dolphins QB Tua Tagovailoa booed loudly in his return to Miami
description: Dolphins fans put everything they had into booing Falcons quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, starting as he came off the sideline for the first series and getting louder from there.
fullText:
MIAMI GARDENS — The first hearty boos were heard at Hard Rock Stadium this football season. And it wasn't even for the Miami Dolphins.

It took one of the more polarizing athletes to come through South Florida in recent years to get the very sparse crowd for Miami's preseason game against the Atlanta Falcons to show some emotion.

Quarterback Tua Tagovailoa, the highest paid player in Dolphins history, returned to his home for the last six years as the Falcons starting quarterback and the fans left no doubt Friday night about how they felt about Tua's time with Miami.

More Miami Dolphins: Can't blame Jeff Hafley for holding out Miami Dolphins starters

For a stadium about one-third full, the crowd put everything it had into letting Tua know how they really feel. The booing started as Tua came off the sideline for the Falcons' first series and got louder as he walked into the huddle and then behind center Corey Levin.

The anticipation was building as Tua dropped back to pass on the first play, but that bubble burst when he completed an 11 yarder to Jahan Dotson. Two more completions, one that Kyle Pitts turned into a 37-yard gain, and Tua was having the last laugh.

Three passes, three completions for 54 yards. Finally, an incompletion when Tua was chased out of the pocket and forced to throw the ball away. Something to cheer.

But that was just the appetizer. Tua led the Falcons to a touchdown on that first drive, but the start of the second drive is what these fans came to see.

Tua walked under center, barked out the play and … muffed the snap. The cheers got louder as Miami's Willie Gay emerged with the ball.

And this wasn't the first time Tua botched a snap on this field. In fact, a mishandled snap led to one of Tua's lowlights while in a Dolphins uniform. After a loss to Arizona in 2024, Tua threw center Aaron Brewer under the bus, saying the snap was not Brewer's "best." That play led to a safety in a one-point loss.

But that was just the start. Tua then turned his ire toward the fans.

"I'd like to see a lot of other people go back there and try to catch that ball, too," he said. "It's not as easy as what it looked like sitting down on your couch eating chips."

Things got worse from there for Tua. Little more than 16 months later, the Dolphins released the man who they handed $167.1 million guaranteed in the summer of 2024.

The Falcons are hoping to find some reward with very little risk, signing Tua for one year and $1.3 million, the veteran minimum.

Tua practically was handed the Falcons starting job — at least early on — with expected starter Michael Penix recovering from a torn ACL suffered in Week 11 last season.

But his training camp struggles had some cracking he was losing that job to air. Penix suddenly re-emerged as a possible Week 1 starter after he was fully cleared for 11-on-11 team drills and all football activities the week of the final preseason game.

Coach Kevin Stefanski must be feeling a bit better about Tua after he completed all but one of his eight passes for 95 yards in his only quarter against the Dolphins. His 116.1 QBR was better than all but two of his 14 games in his final season with Miami.

Tua was sharp on the drive after the fumble, completing four consecutive passes for 41 yards before Brian Robinson's fumble ended the drive.

Cooper Rush replaced Tua on the Falcons' first possession of the second quarter.

As for Tua, he will be associated with failure as much as any athlete to come through South Florida.

He had the weight of the franchise on his shoulders with the slogan — Tank For Tua — for an entire rebuild centered around the man expected to be the savior.

After six mostly painful years marred by injuries and a bloated contract that can only be blamed on former GM Chris Grier, the Dolphins cut ties. So desperate was this franchise to move on that it took a NFL record cap hit of $99.2 million spread over two years.

He will be the highest paid player on the Dolphins' books in 2026 and 2027.

Tua Tagovailoa's time with Miami is done. But he remains the face of two Dolphins rebuilding projects. The one started with his arrival and the one started with his departure.

Tom D'Angelo is a senior sports columnist and reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at tdangelo@pbpost.com.

title: Bob Myers shares which veteran urged him to keep Golden State's core intact
description: Former Warriors GM Bob Myers recently shared a story about a veteran urging him to keep Golden State's core intact following a playoff loss (2013-14).
fullText:
Bob Myers, the executive given the most credit for Golden State's four NBA championships from the 2014-15 season to the 2021-22 season, recently took the time to join NBA Hall of Famers Tracy McGrady and Vince Carter on their podcast. Throughout the duration of the episode, Myers revealed many stories throughout his career, discussing what factors led to him leaving the team, what he misses most about the role and the toughest decision he had to make when in charge.

Additionally, Myers shared a story about a veteran player that urged him to keep the roster in tact prior to their eventual dynasty. After winning 51 games during the 2013-14 campaign and losing to the Los Angeles Clippers in Game 7 of the first round of the Western Conference Playoffs, Myers revealed that he received a call from one of the team's most influential veterans, saying, "Jermaine calls me three days after we lost, and I'm thinking he's going to tell me he's retired and whatever. He goes, 'Hey man, listen to me; do not break this team up.' And I was kind of like, what's so great about this team? We just lost in the first round. And he goes, 'I've been in a lot of locker rooms at the end of a season, and this team knows how to lose.' He said it bothered them the right amount."

While O'Neal, a six-time All-Star in his own right, would retire following an 18-year career after that season, the Warriors would begin a historic dynasty the very next year in the 2014-15 campaign.

fullText:
Four-star shooting guard Chase Lumpkin has narrowed his list of offers to six schools, he told Rivals. Moving forward, the 6-foot-4 rising senior out of McEachern (GA) will consider Alabama, Arkansas, Kentucky, Louisville, Michigan, and USC.

To this point, Lumpkin has completed an official visit to Michigan and unofficially visited Alabama. He's scheduled to take an official visit to USC this weekend, followed by an official visit to Alabama the weekend of September 19th.

Lumpkin is ranked as the No. 30 overall recruit in the 2027 class and the No. 8 ranked point guard, according to the Rivals Industry Ranking, an average of all three major recruiting media companies (Rivals, ESPN, 247Sports).

[ $19.99 gets you a FULL year of On3 | Rivals national coverage ]

In addition to his finalists, he also received offers from Auburn, Georgia Tech, Florida State, Ole Miss, Georgia, Tennessee, Oregon, Providence, UCLA, Indiana, Miami, Iowa, Vanderbilt, UConn, and others.

This summer on the Nike EYBL Circuit, Lumpkin averaged 17.3 points, 5.7 rebounds, 4.5 assists, and 2.2 steals per game for Jet Academy.

He previously spoke with Rivals about what he's looking for in a school.

"I really need to go somewhere I can develop the most and get to the next level and become a pro player, where I've got belief in the coaching staff and they've got belief in me. I just want to get to the next level."

Rivals national recruiting analyst Jamie Shaw has evaluated Lumpkin multiple times in person this summer. Here is what he's written about the highly regarded guard:

"Lumpkin is very confident on the ball. He has good feet and solid positional size in the 6-foot-4 range. He shot the cover off the ball, stepping into shots and knocking down catch and shoots. Also showed passing acumen, delivering on target and on time as a primary initiator. Lumpkin played a streamlined and confident game. He got to spots and put consistent pressure on the opposing team. Lumpkin finished with 29 points and 8 assists on 8 of 15 shooting in the Jet Academy win.

"Lumpkin was the breakout player of the weekend. The Jet Academy guard did a little bit of everything for his team, initiating offense, finishing plays, and generally creating advantages for his team. He showcased excellent vision on the ball, and he processed quickly and efficiently, whether that was getting the ball to his teammates or making shots on his own accord. Lumpkin got into the paint consistently, and he finished well at the rim."

title: Chris Bell's injury in the past as he rolls for Dolphins in preseason
description: Miami Dolphins rookie receiver Chris Bell made his pro debut in a preseason game with Atlanta. Bell looks ready to play.
fullText:
MIAMI GARDENS ― When the Miami Dolphins drafted wide receiver Chris Bell, they hoped he would be available at some point this season.

Bell made his NFL debut in a presason game against the Atlanta Falcons on Friday night, Aug. 28.

It was clear from the start that head coach Jeff Hafley wanted to get a sense for how ready Bell is, after having last season ended with an ACL tear.

The Dolphins targeted Bell five times in the first quarter. He caught two passes for 22 yards, including an 18-yarder from quarterback Cam Miller.

Bell, who played last season at Louisville, is a unique weapon.

He was a third-rounder but would have been at least a second-rounder if not hurt.

Bell is 6-foot-2, 228 pounds. He's fast. And tough. And strong.

"I think he got a lot of savviness to him," Dolphins cornerback JuJu Brents said at the end of training camp. "He a big dude, but he got some stuff about him that you see in like a shorter receiver, so I think he'll be a good complement to all the other receivers we got."

"He looks great," Dolphins tight end Greg Dulcich added. "Routes look awesome. He's a stud."

It's possible Bell has as many targets from Malik Willis this season as Malik Washington, Caleb Douglas, Kevin Coleman Jr., Greg Dulcich or De'Von Achane.

The Dolphins do not figure to have a dominant WR1. It figures the ball will be spread out.

Miami likes that Bell can break tackles.

"I just love his play style," Hafley said near the end of training camp. "He plays with a violence to him, at least looking back at his college tape. He's an explosive player with size."
